task: Fix the certificate validation failure after the root CA was rotated.

candidate_memories.content: mTLS connections to partner services fail with unknown CA error after the root CA was rotated on May 15.
The trust store in /etc/ssl/certs/custom_ca.pem must be updated with the new root CA certificate.
The new root CA was issued by the PKI team and is available in the internal PKI portal.
The old root CA expired on May 15 and is no longer valid; partner services enforce the new CA.
Session 2 note: the infrastructure team flagged failing mTLS handshakes in the service mesh error logs.
mTLS is used for all inter-service communication in the production environment.
Session 6 note: the PKI team completed the annual certificate rotation for all leaf certificates.
Old practice: root CA updates required manual trust store updates on each service host.
The certificate trust store is managed by Puppet and is distributed to all nodes automatically.
Session 11 note: the security team added certificate expiry alerting with 30-day advance notice.
Old CA guide: the old root CA had a 5-year validity period; the new CA has a 3-year period.
Root CA rotations must be tested with a shadow CA period before the old CA expires.
Session 4 note: a TLS configuration audit found no cipher suite violations across all services.
Partner services perform strict certificate pinning and reject certificates from unexpected CAs.
Session 8 note: the Puppet module for trust store management was upgraded to support multiple CAs.
The internal PKI portal provides CRL distribution points for certificate revocation.
Trust store updates must be deployed before the old CA expires to prevent connection failures.
Session 3 note: the networking team added a certificate health check to the monitoring suite.
Old Puppet config: the trust store was updated as a one-time step when the first root CA was deployed.
mTLS client certificates are rotated quarterly; the root CA rotation is on a 3-year cycle.
